citations.text: The scan shows the 包部 heading and 包 bāo headword, followed by a glyph sequence labeled Shuowen small seal, Qin, Han, and regular script forms. Zhou Baohong calls 包 a 会意字 and quotes Shuowen’s account of a pregnant person with 巳 inside as an unformed child. He reads 勹 as wrapping, 巳 as an unborn child, and the pair as conveying 胞衣 (fetal membrane/placenta). He notes 包 is absent from Shang and Western Zhou writing in his view, while its use in the Shijing supports a Western Zhou-era character. The actual printed page number 804 is visible in the scan; the corpus had null printed-page metadata. These are the author’s claims, not independent confirmation of early graph history.

citations.text: Visually checked the printed page number 804, 包部 heading, 包 bāo headword, and the full entry through Zhou Baohong’s attribution. Zhou calls 包 a 会意字, quotes Shuowen’s account of pregnancy, reads 勹 as wrapping and 巳 as an unborn child, and says their combination conveys 胞衣. He says 包 is absent from Shang and Western Zhou writing in his account, while its use in the Shijing indicates that the character should have existed in the Western Zhou. This is Zhou’s interpretation and dating proposal, not independent confirmation of an attested Western Zhou graph.

citations.text: The scan labels a glyph sequence 《说文》小篆, 秦, 睡甲, 汉, 《篆隶表》, and 楷书. These are labels and bibliography citations in 字源; this inspection did not identify or independently verify the glyph specimens against dated artifacts. The 包 entry ends before the separate 胞 headword. The immediately following 胞 discussion says 包 arose roughly in Western Zhou and 胞 in Warring States–Han, a separate 包/胞 account, not evidence for 勹’s role in 包.
